summary:
I added a structure-aware reordering step to MemoryRAG.search(), applied right after the cross-encoder. It runs in hybrid mode only, when the graph channel is active and the reranker actually ran. It has four parts, all gated by a "relevance band": candidates whose reranker logit is within 3.0 of the best one.
(d) graph: relevant candidates that are sources of a cued, currently valid graph path move to the front.
(b) validity: a memory whose graph edges were all closed before now gives its place to its successor, i.e. the memory holding the currently valid edge with the same subject and predicate. The successor is added to the pool before reranking if no channel found it.
(c) versions: for questions with a current cue ("now", "latest", "after the change"), the newer of two relevant statements by the same speaker that share a content word of the question goes first. For history cues ("originally", "before", "first said") the older one goes first. Neutral questions are left alone.
(a) chain: the other memories of a relevant candidate's cued path are placed right after it.
Dev split (hybrid_full): Recall@5 95.8% to 99.4%, MRR 0.905 to 0.962, correct_top1 73.5% to 91.6%, grounded 90.0% to 92.2%, with no per-type regression in any sub-change. Test split, computed once after freezing (hybrid_full): Recall@5 93.0% to 96.1%, MRR 0.904 to 0.948, top-1 77.3% to 89.1% (29 wins, 0 losses), grounded 89.3% to 90.4%. Temporal top-1 went 27.3% to 63.6%, historical 52.2% to 91.3%, conflict 54.5% to 77.3%, recency 43.5% to 65.2%, and multi-hop Recall@5 68.2% to 93.2%. On LoCoMo (3 conversations), Recall@5/10, Hit@5 and pool hit are unchanged. MRR@5 for hybrid_reranked moved 0.5052 to 0.5040 (2 questions down, 0 up).
root_cause:
The cross-encoder (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) scores each (query, snippet) pair on its own text. After reranking, search() sorted only by that score, which threw away three signals the system already had.
1. Graph structure. The graph channel finds cued paths, e.g. Priya-works_at->Tidewater-based_in->Rotterdam. The first-hop memory ("I joined Tidewater Labs") does not mention the city, so the reranker scores it near -4 to -5 and pushes it out of the top 5. For temporal and historical questions, the memory behind the direct path (e.g. "We moved to Oslo" for "Which city does Jonas live in?") lost to text-similar distractors like "My brother lives in Leeds" or "Ingrid lives in Bergen".
2. Validity time. Memories whose explicit relations are closed (valid_to in the past) are textually just as relevant as the current fact, and often more so ("I've been renting a flat in Lisbon" vs "we moved to Porto").
3. Statement order. A correction like "Scratch that, ... moved to Smak" scores lower than the original statement it corrects (7.85 vs 3.78 on dev q-p02-conflict-2), because the original is the cleaner answer to the question.
Diagnostic finding: bge-small content cosine cannot tell supersession pairs (0.44 to 0.76) from unrelated statements by the same persona (job/occupation pairs at 0.73, hq/job pairs at 0.72). So "near-duplicate by cosine" does not work as the topic test for (c). I used the reranker itself as the topicality judge (both in the band) plus a lexical check that both statements share a content word of the question.

proposed_changes.description: Adds time_intent() (history/current/neutral query cues) and _topic_terms(). Adds class attributes MemoryRAG.structure_steps (default {'graph','validity','versions','chain'}; set to frozenset() to switch everything off and get exactly the old behaviour) and MemoryRAG.structure_band = 3.0, in reranker logit units. search() keeps its signature and existing result fields. When structure is active it does two things. Before reranking, it adds successors of stale pool members to the pool (fusion_score 0.0, signals {}), but only for present-tense, non-history queries. After an applied rerank, it calls _structured_order(). Each hit then gets one new field, 'ordering': {'time_intent': ..., 'adjustments': [...]}; adjustments are e.g. graph_path, supersedes:<id>, newer_version_of:<id>, older_version_of:<id>, chain_partner_of:<id>. Two private helpers are added: _validity() runs SQL over the edges table (edges as known now; stale = every edge closed before now; successor = the current same-subject, same-predicate, same-polarity edge whose valid_from is closest to the stale edge's valid_to; also returns the set of memories with currently valid edges). _structured_order() keys each candidate by (graph tier, reranker score). 'B takes A's place' gives B a key just above A's. A final pass inserts path partners after relevant anchors. Arms without the graph channel or without reranking (vector, vector_reranker, vector_graph, hybrid with rerank=False, keyword/semantic/graph/recency modes) are unchanged.

+def time_intent(query, now=None):
+    """Classify the temporal reading a query asks for: 'history', 'current', or 'neutral'.
+
+    History cues ask for an earlier state ("originally", "before", "in 2024"); current cues ask
+    for the latest one ("now", "these days", "most recent"). Both or neither means neutral.
+    """

+    year = (now or utc_now()).year
+    history = bool(_HISTORY_CUES.search(lowered)) or any(
+        int(match) < year for match in _PAST_YEAR.findall(lowered))
+    current = bool(_CURRENT_CUES.search(lowered))
+    if history != current:
+        return 'history' if history else 'current'
+    return 'neutral'

+    def _validity(self, user_id, identifiers, allowed):
+        """Classify candidates by the validity of the graph edges they assert, as currently known.
+
+        stale: every edge the memory asserts was closed before now; maps to the memories holding
+        the currently valid edge with the same subject and predicate (its successors), choosing the
+        edge whose start is closest to the stale edge's end. current: memories with a valid edge now.
+        """
+        now = iso(utc_now())
+        known = 'known_from<=? AND (known_to IS NULL OR known_to>?)'
+        placeholders = ','.join('?' for _ in identifiers)
+        with self.database.connect() as db:
+            rows = [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
+                f'SELECT source_id,subject,predicate,positive,valid_from,valid_to FROM edges '
+                f'WHERE user_id=? AND {known} AND source_id IN ({placeholders})',
+                [user_id, now, now, *identifiers])]
+            by_source = {}
+            for row in rows:
+                by_source.setdefault(row['source_id'], []).append(row)
+            current = {source for source, edges in by_source.items()
+                       if any(edge['valid_from'] <= now and (edge['valid_to'] is None or edge['valid_to'] > now)
+                              for edge in edges)}
+            stale = {}
+            for source, edges in by_source.items():
+                if any(edge['valid_to'] is None or edge['valid_to'] > now for edge in edges):
+                    continue
+                successors = []
+                for edge in edges:
+                    options = [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
+                        f'SELECT source_id,valid_from FROM edges WHERE user_id=? AND subject=? AND predicate=? '
+                        f'AND positive=? AND source_id<>? AND valid_from>=? AND valid_from<=? '
+                        f'AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to>?) AND {known}',
+                        (user_id, edge['subject'], edge['predicate'], edge['positive'], source,
+                         edge['valid_from'], now, now, now, now))]
+                    options = [option for option in options if option['source_id'] in allowed]
+                    if options:
+                        end = datetime.fromisoformat(edge['valid_to'])
+                        gap = lambda option: abs((datetime.fromisoformat(option['valid_from']) - end).total_seconds())
+                        best = min(map(gap, options))
+                        successors += sorted(option['source_id'] for option in options if gap(option) == best)
+                stale[source] = list(dict.fromkeys(successors))
+        return {'stale': stale, 'current': current}
 
+    def _structured_order(self, query, ordered, reranker_scores, paths, by_id, validity, *, intent, present):
+        """Reorder reranked candidates with graph structure and time, which the cross-encoder ignores.
+
+        Each candidate is keyed by (graph tier, reranker score). "B takes A's place" gives B a key
+        just above A's, so B moves directly ahead of A and nothing else changes position.
+          graph:    relevant candidates that source a cued, valid graph path rank first.
+          validity: a stale statement yields its place to the statement that superseded it.
+          versions: for "now"/"latest" (or "originally"/"before") questions, the newer (older) of two
+                    relevant statements by the same speaker about the same query topic goes first.
+          chain:    the other memories of a relevant candidate's cued path follow it directly.
+        """
+        steps = self.structure_steps
+        position = {identifier: index for index, identifier in enumerate(ordered)}
+        top = max(reranker_scores[identifier] for identifier in ordered)
+        relevant = {identifier for identifier in ordered
+                    if reranker_scores[identifier] >= top - self.structure_band}
+        path_index = {}
+        for path in paths:
+            for identifier in path['source_ids']:
+                path_index.setdefault(identifier, []).append(path)
+        tier = {identifier: int('graph' in steps and identifier in relevant and identifier in path_index)
+                for identifier in ordered}
+        key = {identifier: (tier[identifier], reranker_scores[identifier]) for identifier in ordered}
+        notes = {identifier: (['graph_path'] if tier[identifier] else []) for identifier in ordered}
+
+        def take_place(winner, loser, note):
+            target = (key[loser][0], key[loser][1] + 1e-6)
+            if key[winner] < target:
+                key[winner] = target
+                notes[winner].append(f'{note}:{loser}')
+                return True
+            return False
+
+        if 'validity' in steps and present and intent != 'history':
+            for identifier in sorted(validity['stale'], key=lambda item: key.get(item, (-1, 0)), reverse=True):
+                if identifier in key:
+                    for successor in validity['stale'][identifier]:
+                        if successor in key:
+                            take_place(successor, identifier, 'supersedes')
+        if 'versions' in steps and present and intent != 'neutral':
+            newer_first = intent == 'current'
+            note = 'newer_version_of' if newer_first else 'older_version_of'
+            members = [identifier for identifier in ordered if identifier in relevant]
+
+            def speaker(identifier):
+                value = by_id[identifier].source_metadata.get('speaker')
+                return value.casefold() if isinstance(value, str) and value else None
+
+            speakers = {identifier: speaker(identifier) for identifier in members}
+            topics = {identifier: _topic_terms(by_id[identifier].content) for identifier in members}
+            query_terms = _topic_terms(query)
+            for _ in range(len(members)):
+                changed = False
+                for incumbent in sorted(members, key=key.get, reverse=True):
+                    for challenger in members:
+                        first, second = by_id[incumbent], by_id[challenger]
+                        # The challenger must be the newer (current) or older (history) statement,
+                        # by the same speaker, and currently ranked behind the incumbent.
+                        if (incumbent == challenger or key[challenger] > key[incumbent]
+                                or speakers[incumbent] != speakers[challenger]
+                                or first.created_at == second.created_at
+                                or (second.created_at > first.created_at) != newer_first):
+                            continue
+                        # Two statements that both assert currently valid graph relations are
+                        # both true now; neither is a version of the other.
+                        if incumbent in validity['current'] and challenger in validity['current']:
+                            continue
+                        # Same topic: both statements contain a content word of the question.
+                        shared = (query_terms - tokenize(speakers[incumbent] or '')) & topics[incumbent] & topics[challenger]
+                        if shared:
+                            changed |= take_place(challenger, incumbent, note)
+                if not changed:
+                    break
+        ranked = sorted(ordered, key=lambda identifier: (-key[identifier][0], -key[identifier][1], position[identifier]))
+        if 'chain' in steps:
+            chained, placed = [], set()
+            for identifier in ranked:
+                if identifier in placed:
+                    continue
+                chained.append(identifier)
+                placed.add(identifier)
+                if identifier not in relevant:
+                    continue
+                for path in sorted(path_index.get(identifier, []), key=lambda path: len(path['edges'])):
+                    for partner in path['source_ids']:
+                        if partner not in placed and partner in position:
+                            chained.append(partner)
+                            placed.add(partner)
+                            notes[partner].append(f'chain_partner_of:{identifier}')
+            ranked = chained
+        return ranked, {identifier: values for identifier, values in notes.items() if values}
+

proposed_changes.description: New test file with 5 tests, using deterministic fakes (a 2-d embedder and a scripted reranker). (1) A stale statement yields its place to its successor, and the successor is added to the pool even though no channel retrieved it (signals {}, fusion_score 0.0, a real reranker score). (2) A history cue keeps the stale statement and pulls in no successor; rerank=False adds no 'ordering' field and no successor. (3) Versions follow the query's time intent: 'now' puts the newer first, 'originally' the older, neutral leaves the order alone, and a different speaker is never reordered. (4) A graph-path source and its chain partner outrank a text-only distractor; channels=('keyword','semantic') stays unchanged. (5) time_intent() cases, including 'after the schedule change', 'first say', a past vs future year, and a query with both cues. The full file is at the path in this proposal's scratch copy: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephremingstonl-Downloads-code-capstone/2d91e859-4acd-4fbf-99c1-146f2e2aa197/scratchpad/design/rerank/repo/tests/test_structured_rerank.py (diff: .../rerank/out/test_final.diff).

+"""Post-rerank structural ordering: graph evidence, validity, statement versions, evidence chains."""
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+import unittest
+
+from main.domain.models import MemoryRecord
+from main.retrieval.rag import MemoryRAG, time_intent
+from main.storage.store import LocalMemoryStore
+
+
+class Embedder:
+    """Everything is similar to the query except texts naming Porto (orthogonal, below the 0.35 floor)."""
+    model_id = 'structure-test-embedder'
+    dimension = 2
+
+    def passages(self, texts):
+        return [self.query(text) for text in texts]
+
+    def query(self, text):
+        return [0.0, 1.0] if 'Porto' in text else [1.0, 0.0]
+
+
+class ScriptedReranker:
+    """Scores a document by the first scripted phrase it contains; unknown documents score -5."""
+    model_id = 'scripted-reranker'
+
+    def __init__(self, script):
+        self.script = script
+
+    def rerank(self, query, documents):
+        return [next((score for phrase, score in self.script.items() if phrase in text), -5.0)
+                for text in documents]
+
+
+def record(identifier, content, created, *, speaker=None, entities=(), relations=()):
+    metadata = {'entities': list(entities), 'relations': list(relations)}
+    if speaker:
+        metadata['speaker'] = speaker
+    when = created.isoformat()
+    return MemoryRecord.from_dict({
+        'id': identifier, 'content': content, 'user_id': 'u', 'session_id': 's', 'role': 'user',
+        'category': 'semantic', 'tier': 'long_term', 'created_at': when, 'updated_at': when,
+        'recorded_at': when, 'confidence': 1.0, 'importance_score': 0.8, 'source_metadata': metadata})
+
+
+def day(year, month, number=1):
+    return datetime(year, month, number, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+
+
+LISBON = {'id': 'loc:lisbon', 'type': 'location', 'label': 'Lisbon'}
+PORTO = {'id': 'loc:porto', 'type': 'location', 'label': 'Porto'}
+
+
+class StructuredOrderingTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        temporary = TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
+        self.store = LocalMemoryStore(Path(temporary.name) / 'memories.jsonl')
+
+    def rag(self, records, script):
+        self.store._append(records)
+        return MemoryRAG(self.store, embedder=Embedder(), reranker=ScriptedReranker(script), ann_enabled=False)
+
+    def ids(self, hits):
+        return [hit['memory_id'] for hit in hits]
+
+    def homes(self):
+        return [
+            record('old-home', 'I have been renting a flat in Lisbon since 2021', day(2024, 1),
+                   entities=[LISBON], relations=[{'subject': 'self', 'predicate': 'lives_in', 'object': 'loc:lisbon',
+                                                  'valid_from': day(2021, 4).isoformat(),
+                                                  'valid_to': day(2025, 3, 15).isoformat()}]),
+            record('new-home', 'We finally moved to Porto last March', day(2025, 6),
+                   entities=[PORTO], relations=[{'subject': 'self', 'predicate': 'lives_in', 'object': 'loc:porto',
+                                                 'valid_from': day(2025, 3, 15).isoformat()}]),
+            record('noise', 'I have a flat white every morning', day(2024, 2)),
+        ]
+
+    def test_stale_statement_yields_its_place_to_the_successor(self):
+        rag = self.rag(self.homes(), {'Lisbon': 5.0, 'flat white': 4.0, 'Porto': -6.0})
+        hits = rag.search('Which town am I in?', user_id='u', limit=3)
+        self.assertEqual(self.ids(hits), ['new-home', 'old-home', 'noise'])
+        self.assertIn('supersedes:old-home', hits[0]['ordering']['adjustments'])
+        # No channel retrieved the successor; it joined the reranked pool through the graph.
+        self.assertEqual(hits[0]['signals'], {})
+        self.assertEqual(hits[0]['fusion_score'], 0.0)
+        self.assertEqual(hits[0]['reranker_score'], -6.0)
+        self.assertEqual(hits[0]['candidate_pool_size'], 3)
+
+    def test_history_cues_and_disabled_reranking_keep_the_stale_statement(self):
+        rag = self.rag(self.homes(), {'Lisbon': 5.0, 'flat white': 4.0, 'Porto': -6.0})

+    def test_versions_follow_the_time_intent_of_the_question(self):

+        now = rag.search("Which day is Priya's retro on now?", user_id='u', limit=3)
+        self.assertEqual(self.ids(now), ['retro-new', 'retro-old', 'retro-other'])
+        self.assertIn('newer_version_of:retro-old', now[0]['ordering']['adjustments'])

Regression watch (dev):
- Historical queries (as_of set): validity and versions are off. Graph promotion improves top-1 from 3/7 to 6/7.
- Conflict queries asking for the original value (q-p01-conflict-3 "Before it was corrected...", q-p03-conflict-3 "...first say..."): both flip from wrong to correct under the history intent.
- Episodic questions about older events: 7/7 top-1 kept. q-p02-episodic-3 "Which language exam did Jonas register to take?" is neutral, so it is left alone. When neutral queries were also reordered newer-first, this query lost top-1 (episodic 100 to 85.7); that is why the variant was rejected.

Design choices tuned on dev, using offline simulation of captured pools (sim.py, policies2.py); the simulation matched the harness exactly.
- Band margin swept over 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 logits and over probability ratios 0.5, 0.33, 0.2. Top-1 by margin: 85.5 / 89.2 / 90.4 / 89.2 / 91.6 / 86.7 (before the cue-regex fix). Margins 2 to 5 are flat. Margins of 4 or more start graph-promoting false cues ("How does Amara prefer..." to pref_new) and letting the lexical topic test fire on generic words ("home" in "came home"). Chose 3.
- A separate, wider band for versions (5) fixed q-p02-conflict-2 but broke q-p03-temporal-1: net 0, rejected.
- Cosine-floor topic test: rejected (see root cause). Skipping pairs where both memories hold currently valid relations: kept; no dev change, but principled.
- Chain completion limited to the terminal hop: identical on dev; kept 'any path' as the spec describes.
- The successor takes the stale memory's place but does not inherit graph promotion. An earlier variant that let it inherit broke q-p01-semantic-1 and q-p03-multi_hop-2 top-1.

risks:
1. Cue lexicons are English heuristics. "before <date>" and "in <year>" count as history cues even when they are date anchors (LoCoMo q133 lost rank). A hypothetical "still" counts as a current cue (LoCoMo q14). Neutral questions get no version ordering, so a neutral "Where is my sister's wedding?" with an old and a corrected statement keeps the reranker order. On dev, reordering neutral queries cost an older-event episodic query.
2. The lexical topic test (both statements share a content word of the question) can fire on generic words: "home" matched "came home" when tried with a wider band. The 3-logit band and the same-speaker requirement contain this, but it can mis-order same-speaker statements that share an incidental word under current or history cues. Unrelated pairs that both hold currently valid graph relations are protected.
3. Graph promotion trusts graph_predicates() cues, which are noisy ("like explanations" cues likes; "while working" cues works_at). The reranker band is the only guard, so a cued path source within 3 logits of the top can displace a better text match. Inside the graph tier, order is still by reranker score, so 1-hop vs 2-hop ambiguity remains (dev q-p02-temporal-2).
4. structure_band is in raw logit units of the shipped MS MARCO cross-encoder. An injected reranker with a different scale (e.g. probabilities) would make the band include everything.
5. Validity depends on explicit valid_to or supersession-closed graph edges. Memories without relations are untouched, and claims extracted from content create open edges that make a memory count as not stale. The successor rule picks the current same-subject, same-predicate edge whose start is closest to the stale edge's end; with multi-valued predicates such as likes, an unrelated current like could be chosen.
6. Successors added to the pool carry fusion_score 0.0 and signals {}. Downstream code that assumes every hit came from some channel should tolerate that. candidate_pool_size can exceed candidate_limit by the number of successors.
7. Dev is small (83 answerable queries). The band and the design choices were picked on dev using a flat region of the sweep. The test confirmed the gains (29/0 top-1 wins), but the test personas follow the same templates as dev, so external generalisation is only weakly evidenced: LoCoMo, which has no explicit relations, is neutral.
8. Latency was not isolated because of concurrent load. Expect a small extra cost: 1 + (#stale edges) SQL queries and an O(pool^2) pair loop.
